text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Visiting Prince Kiril, son of Bulgaria's exiled king Simeon II and an economic advisor to President Petar Stoyanov discussed Bulgaria's privatisation programme with the president.
-- Bulgaria's Fair Competition Commissiion (FCC) fined Germany's Westdeutsche Algemeine Zeitung (WAZ) for unfair competition, a FCC official said. @
WAZ holds 70 percent stakes in Bulgaria's two largest press groups, which have a total of 74.6 percent share in the local newspaper market.
-- South Korea's Daewoo Corp. is interested in setting up a car assembly plant in Bulgaria, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov said.
-- Bulgaria's state National Television said it needed some 21 billion levs to broadcast 7,000 hours of programme by the end-1997.
-- The European Investment Bank is expected to extend $3.5 million to Bulgaria's Telecommunication Company (BTC) to upgrade BTC equipment, private Balkan news agency said.
-- Bulgaria's parliament elected former interim Finance minister Svetoslav Gavriiski as a governor of the Bulgarian National Bank to operate under a currency board system.
-- Bulgaria expects over $650 million of foreign investment this year, Foreign Investment Agency executive director Iliyan Vassilev said. @

-- Bulgaria hopes to seal a preliminary contract for the sale of 56 percent of MDK copper smelter to Belgium's Union Miniere within two months, Privatisation Agency executive director Alexander Sabotinov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
